svg.text: LM-137 TO LM-140 - POSTCOMMUNION, DISMISSAL, LAST GOSPEL, LEONINE PRAYERS
1962 Low Mass ending - with official 1962 dismissal branches

g.text: LM-137A/C - COMMUNION ANTIPHON AND POSTCOMMUNION
1. Priest reads Communion antiphon at Epistle-side missal, hands joined.
2. Return center - hands on altar - kiss - turn right.
3. Dominus vobiscum; servers answer Et cum spiritu tuo.
4. Turn left back to altar and return to the Epistle-side missal.
AT EACH OREMUS
extend hands - bow to cross - join - immediately extend again.
Read Postcommunion prayer(s) with hands extended.
LENTEN FERIAL BRANCH
Ash Wednesday through Wednesday of Holy Week:
Oremus - Humiliate capita vestra Deo - Oratio super populum.
LM-138A/B - FINAL SALUTATION AND 1962 DISMISSAL
Priest returns center - altar kiss - turns right - Dominus vobiscum.
NORMAL 1962 MASS
Ite, missa est - facing the people. Server: Deo gratias.
Important: NOT conditioned on whether Gloria was said.
PROCESSION / OTHER FUNCTION FOLLOWS
Benedicamus Domino - facing altar. No blessing. No Last Gospel.
REQUIEM
Requiescant in pace - facing altar. Server: Amen. No blessing.
Last Gospel omitted if absolution over catafalque follows.
LM-138C/D - PLACEAT AND LAST BLESSING
PLACEAT TIBI
medium body bow; joined hands on altar edge; prayer in low voice.
Then palms on altar - kiss - stand erect.
BENEDICAT VOS
eyes to cross; extend/elevate/join/lower hands; bow at Deus.
Turn right; left hand on breast; large cross over people.
Complete rightward circle back toward altar; go to Gospel side.
SERVERS
simple bow at Benedicat vos omnipotens Deus; sign themselves; Amen.
Then both stand for Last Gospel.
LM-139A/B - LAST GOSPEL
Priest faces same direction as at the first Gospel.
Dominus vobiscum, hands joined.
Left hand open on altar; right thumb signs altar, forehead, lips, breast.
Servers sign forehead, lips, breast in unison and answer Gloria tibi Domine.
ET VERBUM CARO FACTUM EST
Priest places hands on altar and genuflects toward Last Gospel card.
Both servers genuflect in unison.
At conclusion servers answer Deo gratias, then come together at center.
1962 SPECIALS
Ordinary: John 1:1-14. Palm Sunday has a proper branch.
Several specified Masses omit the Last Gospel entirely.
LM-140A/B - LEONINE PRAYERS (POST-MASS APPENDIX)
After Last Gospel, priest descends slightly Gospel-side and kneels.
Both acolytes kneel in plano, one level below and slightly behind him.
SEQUENCE
3 Ave Maria - Salve Regina - versicle/response - prayer for Church
and conversion of sinners - St Michael - Sacred Heart invocation x3.
SERVER POSTURE
Servers lead responses. While kneeling with the priest, they do not add
the ordinary standing/kneeling word-bows merely because a name occurs.
Do not fetch a Leonine-prayer card during the Last Gospel.
Leonine prayers are modeled as post-Mass devotion, not Mass proper.
LM-140C - RECESSIONAL
After prayers both acolytes stand immediately.
Both assist the priest with his alb as he ascends to retrieve the chalice.
AC1 retrieves and presents the biretta if one was worn.
Priest descends with veiled chalice.
All genuflect together at the foot.
Acolytes turn inward, meet shoulder-to-shoulder in front of priest,
and lead the recessional to the sacristy.
END OF SPOKEN 1962 LOW MASS PROFILE

svg.text: APPROVED TRANSITION INTO THIS SHEET - CORRECTED ABLUTIONS / COORDINATED TRANSFER
- First: wine, with the chalice remaining on the altar.
- Second: water, with the priest holding the chalice; AC1 steps down exactly one altar step to pour.
After the vessels are cleansed, AC1 and AC2 perform the coordinated transfer:
- AC1 carries the chalice veil / chalice cloth to the Gospel side.
- AC2 carries the missal to the Epistle side.
- First crossing: AC2 in front, AC1 behind.
- Priest receives the chalice cloth on the Gospel side.
- Second crossing: AC1 in front, AC2 behind.
- Both resume their ordinary kneeling positions.
The old pre-1962 shortcut 'no Gloria = Benedicamus Domino' is NOT used. Normal 1962 Masses use Ite, missa est.
Benedicamus Domino remains for a Mass immediately followed by a procession/other function; Requiem uses Requiescant in pace.
